subject: physical-education
title: Investigation or close reading: offense and defense space
essentialQuestion: How can understanding games, strategy, and fair play help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

goal: I can build the target movement from a controlled entry version to a fresh application for offense and defense space, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Eyes up, slow first, stop inside. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Show ready and controlled stop without traveling.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: two soft household objects as pathway markers.
Use imaginary lines, floor points, or seated arm patterns.
movementCues: READY with a balanced base, soft joints, eyes up, and the path clear.
TRAVEL with quiet controlled steps, wheel pushes, or an in-place pattern.
SLOW before changing direction or pathway.
STOP inside the boundary with control.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Use one short action at a time, say the main cue before the attempt, keep the skill development choice concrete, and ask a trusted adult to confirm any required permission or space check.

movementModel.title: Model for offense and defense space
movementModel.startingPosition: Begin behind a visible or imaginary boundary with a stable base and enough room for a controlled stop.
movementModel.action: Travel or gesture along one short pathway, slow before the change, and finish inside the boundary.
movementModel.keyCue: Eyes up, slow first, stop inside.
movementModel.commonError: Looking down or changing direction before reducing pace.
movementModel.correction: Use a fixed eye-level point, shorten the path, and rehearse slow-change-stop in place.
movementModel.notice: Notice spacing, pathway, and controlled start/stop rather than speed.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice spacing, pathway, and controlled start/stop rather than speed.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use no jumping when surface, ceiling, footwear, or support is uncertain; use the in-place route whenever full travel is not safe. No indoor running, uncertain jump, collision path, or movement beyond the cleared boundary.

guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Eyes up, slow first, stop inside.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Use a fixed eye-level point, shorten the path, and rehearse slow-change-stop in place.

guidedPractice.prompt: Travel or gesture along one short straight pathway.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Looking down or changing direction before reducing pace.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice spacing, pathway, and controlled start/stop rather than speed.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: offense and defense space
directions: Choose a fresh pathway and complete or describe ready, travel, slow-change, and controlled stop.
Use this cue or decision: Eyes up, slow first, stop inside.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Use the complete cue sequence in a new learner-chosen safe variation. Choose a fresh pathway and complete or describe ready, travel, slow-change, and controlled stop.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Rehearse the start and controlled stop in place.
Trace the pathway change at a comfortable pace.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear a dry non-slip path of two arm-spans when available. Low-space route: stay within one arm-span seated, supported, standing, or using a mobility aid. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: two soft household objects as pathway markers.
householdSubstitutes: Use imaginary lines, floor points, or seated arm patterns.
prohibited: No indoor running, uncertain jump, collision path, or movement beyond the cleared boundary.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm/wheel-path gestures to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use no jumping when surface, ceiling, footwear, or support is uncertain; use the in-place route whenever full travel is not safe.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Eyes up, slow first, stop inside. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for offense and defense space, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for offense and defense space.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Eyes up, slow first, stop inside. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm/wheel-path gestures to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm/wheel-path gestures to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Choose a fresh pathway and complete or describe ready, travel, slow-change, and controlled stop. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm/wheel-path gestures to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions.

evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.

diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for offense and defense space; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Show ready and controlled stop without traveling.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Eyes up, slow first, stop inside.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Looking down or changing direction before reducing pace. — with this correction — Use a fixed eye-level point, shorten the path, and rehearse slow-change-stop in place.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Travel or gesture along one short straight pathway.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Choose a fresh pathway and complete or describe ready, travel, slow-change, and controlled stop. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice spacing, pathway, and controlled start/stop rather than speed. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.
